name: Shirley MacLaine
milestone_by_age_26: Made her film debut in Alfred Hitchcock's The Trouble with Harry (1955) at age 21 and won the Golden Globe Award for New Star of the Year – Actress, launching a major Hollywood career.
early_history_summary: Raised in Richmond, Virginia by a drama-teacher mother and psychology-professor father, MacLaine trained in ballet from age three and attended the Washington School of Ballet. At 17 she spent the summer performing in a subway-circuit production of Oklahoma! in New York, and after high school graduation she made her Broadway debut in the chorus of Me and Juliet (1953). She became understudy to Carol Haney in The Pajama Game; when Haney broke her ankle in May 1954, MacLaine took over the role and was spotted by Jerry Lewis, who urged producer Hal B. Wallis to sign her to a Paramount Pictures contract.
family_context_summary: Born into a middle-class Virginia family; father Ira Beaty was a psychology professor, school administrator, and realtor; mother Kathlyn was a drama teacher from Nova Scotia who introduced MacLaine to ballet at age three. Younger brother is filmmaker Warren Beatty.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a drama teacher who introduced MacLaine to ballet and theater from age three, providing direct domain immersion and training guidance throughout childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: drama-teacher mother, ballet from age 3, Broadway chorus, Paramount contract, Golden Age Hollywood
evidence_summary: MacLaine's mother, a drama teacher, introduced her to ballet at age three and immersed her in performing arts throughout childhood. After training at the Washington School of Ballet, she moved to New York at 18 and quickly landed Broadway chorus roles, eventually understudying Carol Haney in The Pajama Game. When Haney was injured in 1954, MacLaine's replacement performance was seen by Jerry Lewis and producer Hal B. Wallis, who signed her to a Paramount contract. Her film debut in Hitchcock's The Trouble with Harry (1955) at age 21 earned her a Golden Globe for New Star of the Year, and she received her first Oscar nomination at 24 for Some Came Running (1958).
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Richmond, Virginia; father was a psychology professor and realtor, mother was a drama teacher from Nova Scotia who introduced her to ballet at age three.
current_position: Retired from regular acting but still occasionally appears in films; estimated net worth approximately $50 million; resides in the United States. Most recent notable film role was in The Last Word (2017).

name: Vijay Singh
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1984 Malaysian PGA Championship at age 21, his first professional tournament victory, after turning professional in 1982. He was also Fiji amateur champion at age 17 in 1980.
early_history_summary: Born in Lautoka, Fiji to an Indo-Fijian family, Singh learned golf from his father Mohan, a nine-time club champion at the Nadi Airport Golf Club. He started playing at age 11, practiced obsessively on the airport course after school, and by 16 was winning island competitions. At 17 he was Fiji amateur champion and Airport Club champion. He dropped out of school at 16, turned professional in 1982 at age 19, and won his first professional event at the 1984 Malaysian PGA Championship at age 21.
family_context_summary: Born to an Indo-Fijian family in Lautoka, Fiji; father Mohan Singh was a refueler at Nadi International Airport and a nine-time club champion golfer at the Nadi Airport Golf Club. Two older brothers were also golfers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a nine-time club champion golfer who taught Singh the game from age 11, provided technical advice about modeling his swing after tall and lanky golfers, and gave him access to the Nadi Airport Golf Club.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father taught golf, airport course access, obsessive practice, Fiji amateur champion at 17, turned pro at 19
evidence_summary: Singh grew up in humble circumstances in Fiji, but his father's position as a nine-time club champion at the Nadi Airport Golf Club gave him direct access to the course and expert instruction from age 11. He practiced obsessively, hitting hundreds of balls daily, and by 17 was Fiji amateur champion. He dropped out of school at 16 to focus on golf, turned professional at 19, and won his first professional tournament at 21 (1984 Malaysian PGA Championship). His path was driven by extreme self-created repetition rather than elite academies or networks, and his isolation in Fiji was both a constraint and a catalyst for his legendary work ethic.
starting_point: Born to an Indo-Fijian working-class family in Lautoka, Fiji; father was an airport refueler and accomplished amateur golfer who taught Vijay the game from age 11.
current_position: Playing on PGA Tour Champions; resides in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida; career earnings exceed $70 million; inducted into World Golf Hall of Fame in 2006.

name: Ercole Baldini
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Olympic gold medal in the road race at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics at age 23, also winning the world amateur individual pursuit title and breaking the world hour record (46.394 km) the same year. He had previously set the amateur hour record at 21 in 1954.
early_history_summary: Born in Villanova di Forlì, Italy, Baldini started racing at age 17 in 1950. He took his first major result in 1953 with a third place in the Piccolo Giro di Lombardia. In 1954 at age 21 he set the world amateur hour record with 44.870 km, earning the nickname 'Il Treno di Forlì' (The Forlì Train). His breakthrough year was 1956 when he won Olympic gold in the road race, the world amateur pursuit title, and broke Jacques Anquetil's professional hour record.
family_context_summary: Born in Villanova di Forlì, Italy; the fourth of six sons. Family financial and occupational background is not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Italian cycling heartland, Olympic gold 1956, world hour record, amateur hour record at 21, Forlì Train
evidence_summary: Baldini grew up in Forlì, Italy, in the heartland of professional cycling during its golden era. He started racing at 17 and by 21 had set the world amateur hour record. His exceptional physical ability was evident in his 1956 season at age 23, when he won Olympic gold, the world amateur pursuit title, and broke the professional hour record. Italy's deep cycling infrastructure, including the Velodromo Vigorelli in Milan, provided the facilities and competitive ecosystem that enabled his rapid rise. He turned professional in 1957 and won the Giro d'Italia and world road race championship in 1958.
starting_point: Born in Villanova di Forlì, Italy, the fourth of six sons; family occupational and financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on December 1, 2022 at age 89 in Forlì, Italy; final achievements included 1958 Giro d'Italia winner, world professional road race champion, and Olympic gold medalist.

name: Gheorghe Zamfir
milestone_by_age_26: Won First Prize in a national music contest in 1959 at age 18 and recorded his first compositions with the Folkloric Orchestra of the Romanian Radio Broadcasting Corporation the same year. By age 25 (1966) he was director of the 'Ciocarlia' ensemble with 300 artists and released his first commercial disc on Electrecord.
early_history_summary: Born in Găești, Romania, Zamfir was attracted to music from childhood, initially studying the accordion. At age 14 (1955) his father enrolled him at the Special Musical School no. 1 in Bucharest, where he was assigned to the pan flute class of master Fănică Luca despite initial reluctance. He demonstrated extraordinary ability and within four years won First Prize in a national contest in 1959 and made his first radio recordings. He entered the Ciprian Porumbescu Conservatory in 1961 and by 1966 was director of the 'Ciocarlia' folk ensemble.
family_context_summary: Born in Găești, Romania; parents managed a small grocery store which gave the family considerable status in a centrally planned economy. Father had once owned a vineyard. Mother introduced Zamfir to Romanian folk songs.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother introduced Zamfir to Romanian folk songs during childhood. Father enrolled him in music school at age 14. Parents were not professional musicians but supported his musical education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Fanica Luca mentor, Special Musical School Bucharest, national prize at 18, radio recordings, Ciocarlia ensemble director
evidence_summary: Zamfir grew up in a small Romanian town with parents who managed a grocery store and supported his musical interests. At 14, he was enrolled at the Special Musical School in Bucharest where he was assigned to the pan flute class of Fănică Luca, Romania's foremost nai virtuoso, who became his sustained mentor. Despite initial reluctance, Zamfir showed extraordinary aptitude and within four years won First Prize in a national contest (1959) and recorded with the Romanian Radio Folkloric Orchestra. By 25 he was directing the 'Ciocarlia' ensemble with 300 artists. His mastery of a nearly extinct instrument gave him scarce technical depth that defined his career.
starting_point: Born in Găești, Romania, a small industrial city; parents managed a small grocery store and father had once owned a vineyard, giving the family modest status in communist Romania.
current_position: Still active as a pan flute virtuoso and professor at the National University of Music in Bucharest; resides in Bucharest; known worldwide as 'The Master of the Pan Flute' with over 300 compositions and a career spanning six decades.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at the Special Musical School no. 1 in Bucharest and began studying pan flute under master Fănică Luca, demonstrating extraordinary ability on the instrument.
